Playground main view — resting state
Strategy A “The Ledger”: rank-ordered rows + involvement spine + persistent aggregate band
canvas 1440 x 900
GRAYSCALE STRUCTURE WIREFRAME — no colour, no final type, no motion

g.text: Sprint review, nine people. A colleague is presenting your architecture as their own. The promotion list closes in six days.
session beat 12 · run 2 of this vessel
ACTION SET — HOVER TO FORECAST, CLICK TO COMMIT
5 candidates · one commit ends this scenario
Two sentences and a link, into the silence.
Te not in stack → routed to Ti (+35% cost)
Make them say the architecture out loud.
Smooth it; take it up after
Let the meeting land, then talk privately.
Si not in stack → routed to Ni (+35% cost)
No reaction. The commit history keeps.
suppression is an action, and it is priced
Leave the room before deciding anything.
session · 2 runs · 20 beats retained on screen
reduced-motion: beats land instantly, no jitter

svg.text: CALLOUT LEGEND — WHAT THE REGION DOES · HOV ON HOVER · CMT ON COMMIT · L/G UNDER LOOP OR GRIP
Scenario envelope
A literal container, not a header. The heavy 2.5px frame encloses every readout on the screen, because every
readout is conditioned on this situation. Nothing simulation-related is drawn outside it.
HOV
CMT
Frame persists through commit; the run ends inside it.
L/G
Loop and Grip add a hatched inner rule to the frame so the container itself declares the state.
Scenario identity + reopen briefing
Title, one-line vignette, and a route back to the full briefing (S2) without losing state. The vessel code sits
beside it so the user always knows which psyche they are watching.
HOV
CMT
L/G
State chip + the two margins (answers Q-C)
The distance-to-break readout. One chip naming the current state, then two margin meters: points of accumulated
load remaining before Loop, and before Grip. This is the only always-on predictive readout and it is placed at the
strongest position on the screen.
HOV
Both margins show a dashed forecast segment for the hovered action — this is how a user learns an action would trip a
state before they commit it.
CMT
Margins step to their new values and the chip re-evaluates; a crossing animates as a threshold break, not a smooth
slide.
L/G
Chip inverts to solid dark; the crossed margin reads AT LIMIT and the other becomes the live one.
Function row — height encodes rank
Four rows in stack order, dominant first, at 186 / 156 / 122 / 100px. Rank is carried by physical size and
vertical position, never by colour. The order of the rows is the lesson, so the layout is the lesson.
HOV
No row-level hover state; rows respond to action hover, not pointer position, so the forecast never depends on where
the pointer happens to rest.
CMT
All four rows step one beat together.
L/G
Loop dims and hatches the auxiliary row. Grip swaps the height allocations of the dominant and inferior rows — vertical
order and rank labels stay put, so the labels end up visibly out of order with the sizes, which reads as the hierarchy
being overthrown rather than reordered.
Glyph slot — present, legible, subordinate
The function’s own glyph from its info page, rendered at 32px (dom) / 28 (aux) / 24 (tert) / 22 (inf), pinned
bottom-left of the identity gutter with the glyph name beside it. It occupies roughly 2% of row area. It exists so
a user can map this panel back to the page they studied — it is an index, not the anchor. The anchor is the
two-letter label above it, set at 30px.
HOV
Glyph is inert on hover — it never becomes the interactive target.
CMT
Unchanged.
L/G
Under Grip the inferior’s glyph steps up to 32px, the only time a glyph changes size, marking that the function has
been promoted by force.
Expression stream — the inner voice
That function’s running commentary, newest line at the bottom, older lines fading upward. Line count is the
fidelity tier: 5 lines dominant, 3 auxiliary, 2 tertiary and inferior. At rest this is the only continuously
animating element on the screen.
HOV
A dashed PROJECTED block appears beneath the live lines carrying what this function would say if the hovered action
were committed. The live stream keeps running underneath, unmodified.
CMT
The projected line is promoted into the stream as a real line and the block empties.
L/G
Loop stalls the auxiliary stream mid-sentence and leaves it stalled; Grip replaces the inferior’s register entirely
with crude, absolutist phrasing and gives it 5 lines.
Seismograph — stress over beats
The x-axis is beat index, not seconds. Roughly 16 beats visible; the trace is solid ink for committed history.
Between beats it still moves — decay and small jitter — so the instrument reads as alive without penalising a slow
reader.
HOV
Forecast is drawn only inside the reserved band (callout 8); committed history is never redrawn on hover.
CMT
The forecast segment translates left across NOW and hardens from dashed to solid.
L/G
Loop produces a regular self-reinforcing oscillation between dominant and tertiary; Grip produces a rising trace on the
inferior and flattens the dominant.
NOW rule + reserved forecast band
NOW sits at 72% of the trace width. The rightmost 28% is permanently reserved for forecast and is drawn empty, in
a dashed well, at rest. Nothing committed is ever drawn to the right of NOW. This is the single rule that keeps
projection and record separable without colour.
HOV
The reserved band fills with the hatched forecast and a dashed trace.
CMT
Band empties again immediately after the forecast crosses into history.
L/G
Unchanged — the reservation is structural.
Scalar readout cluster
Pleasure, involvement share, and energy/capacity, stacked in a fixed order in a fixed column so the same readout
is at the same x-position in all four rows. Vertical scanning down one column is the intended comparison gesture.
HOV
Each meter grows a dashed forecast extension or retraction from its committed fill; the capacity meter grows a hatched
segment showing exactly what the action would take.
CMT
Meters animate to their new value once and stop.
L/G
Loop zeroes the auxiliary’s involvement and freezes its stress decay; Grip pushes the inferior’s capacity below zero
into visible DEBT hatching.
Forecast delta gutter — reserved, empty at rest
A dedicated column at the right edge of every row that holds nothing until hover. Deltas are set large; levels
stay small inside the cluster. This implements “deltas over levels”: the change is the content, the level is
context.
HOV
Fills with signed deltas for stress, pleasure, involvement, and energy.
CMT
Empties.
L/G
Under Loop/Grip the gutter also carries a small state-attribution tag when a delta is caused by the state rather than
by the action.
Involvement spine (answers Q-A)
One continuous full-height stacked bar, four segments, summing to 100%. It is the fastest answer to “who is
running this?” — readable peripherally, without reading a number. Because row heights are fixed by rank and spine
segments are sized by involvement, the mismatch between them is itself a readout: a segment taller than its own
row means that function is working above its station, marked with a tick in the left margin. In Grip the inferior
overruns even the doubled row height it has been granted, and that is visible from across the room.
HOV
Segment boundaries show dashed proposed positions for the hovered action; the existing segments stay put so
before/after is legible in one glance.
CMT
Segments animate to the new ratio; the ratio always renormalises to exactly 100%.
L/G
Loop collapses the auxiliary segment to near zero; Grip makes the inferior segment the largest.
Action rail
The candidate reactions, always visible, right-aligned so the pointer is near the per-row delta gutter while
hovering. Five cards at rest. One commit ends the scenario.
HOV
Exactly one card can be hovered; hovering is the only way to see a forecast anywhere on the screen.
CMT
Rail locks and the run advances to resolution (S9).
L/G
Loop and Grip append generated alleviate and aggravate cards to this rail, tagged and sorted after the authored ones.
Action card anatomy
Title, one-line detail, signature chips naming which functions the action demands and in what proportion, a
routing note when it demands a function this stack does not carry, and a likelihood bar.
HOV
Card raises, gains a commit affordance, and drives every forecast on the screen.
CMT
Card is the committed action; its outcome text carries into S9.
L/G
Generated cards carry an ALLEVIATES or AGGRAVATES tag in the top-right.
Whole-Human band (persistent, expandable)
The aggregate lives on this screen permanently as a thin band, so part and whole are visible in the same glance.
Carries the aggregate trace, four aggregate scalars, and the impressions-in / expressions-out balance. Expands in
place into the full S6 apparatus without navigating away.
HOV
Aggregate readouts forecast alongside the four rows, using the same dashed-and-hatched grammar.
CMT
Aggregate steps with the rows.
L/G
The band is where Loop and Grip are most legible as a whole-person event rather than a per-function one.
Teaching overrides + history scope
Manual Loop and Grip toggles, always available regardless of accumulated load, plus history scope and
reduced-motion status. Placed at the bottom because they are instructor controls, not part of the primary loop.
HOV
Toggle preview shows how many readouts would be rewritten.
CMT
Toggling is instantaneous and does not consume a beat or any energy.
L/G
A manually entered state is tagged MANUAL everywhere it is reported, and never satisfies an automatic exit condition —
the user must toggle it back off.
Fidelity tier chip
Declares which tier this row is rendering at: FULL, MID, or LOW. Tier is set by rank at rest and promoted on
focus, and it is what makes twenty simultaneous signals legible without shrinking anything.
HOV
CMT
L/G
Grip promotes the inferior row to FULL and demotes the dominant to MID — the tiering itself is a readout of the state.

Structure phase, grayscale by discipline. Colour, type scale, glyph artwork and motion curves are deferred to the visual-design phase; tick tuning, persistence and the text corpus are deferred to implementation. Both deferral lists are
enumerated in 00-BRIEF.md section 5 and BUILD-SPEC.md section 9. Worked type: ISTP (Ti / Se / Ni / Fe). Worked scenario: The Credit Thief.
